versions.text: Criterion: Verify that each SSSE has sufficient bidirectional traceability established for requirements (performance and interface), design, source code, and test data. Standard: Bidirectional traceability exists from the system level to the element requirement level. Sufficient SSSE bidirectional traceability also exists from the SSSE requirements to the detailed design, and to the source code and all levels of test. SCF bidirectional traceability exists both vertically (system level to the lowest software level) and horizontally (across the system/software). Requirements supporting SCFs are identified (e.g., tagged as safety critical). Bidirectional traceability of all software ensures that unwanted or unapproved code is not present (e.g., unused code, malicious code). Method of Compliance: Verification methods include analysis and inspection of documentation. Verify that requirements have full bidirectional traceability from the system level to the software requirements. Verify that bidirectional traceability also exists for the software design and source code. Full SCF bidirectional traceability (both vertically and horizontally) from the system level to the software design level is verified through inspection of traceability data. Verify through bidirectional traceability that requirements and functions are coupled to all levels of testing. Verify that requirements supporting SCFs are tagged. Verify that no unwanted code exists. Standard: 1. Verify that each ESS has sufficient bidirectional traceability established for requirements (performance and interface), design, implementation, source code, and test data. Bidirectional requirement traceability exists from the air system level to the lowest requirement level. ESS bidirectional traceability also exists from the ESS requirements to the detailed design, and to the implementation and source code and all levels of test. Safety-critical function bidirectional traceability exists both vertically (system level to the lowest level) and horizontally (functionally across the system). Requirements supporting SCFs are tagged with an identifier of the specific SCF(s) supported. Bidirectional traceability of all software ensures that unwanted or unapproved code is not present (e.g., unused code, malicious code). Method of Compliance: Prior to entering flight test, verify the standard by the following method(s): The number next to an MoC line item corresponds to the numbered line item in the standard that is being verified: 1. Verification method includes analysis. Verify that requirements have full bidirectional traceability from the system level to the lowest level requirements. Verify that bidirectional traceability also exists for the ESS design, implementation, and source code. Full SCF bidirectional traceability (both vertically and horizontally) from the system level to the ESS design level is verified through analysis of traceability data. Verify through bidirectional traceability that requirements and functions are coupled to all levels of testing. Verify that requirements supporting SCFs are tagged with an identifier of the specific SCF(s) supported. Verify that no unwanted code exists.
